Q: Ensure macaddr value is unique across columns A:

Exclusion constraints on expressions can enforce custom equality. demo at db<>fiddle

alter table device add constraint mac_unique_across_3_columns
exclude using gist ((array[wifi_mac,ethernet_mac,bluetooth_mac]) with &&);

The index backing up this constraint now holds all 3 values in one array and those are compared using && overlap operator, meaning that all 3 values need to be different across all 3 columns. Otherwise, you get the desired:

ERROR:  conflicting key value violates exclusion constraint "mac_unique_across_3_columns"
DETAIL:  Key ((ARRAY[wifi_mac, ethernet_mac, bluetooth_mac]))=({12189697,12189700,12189701}) conflicts with existing key ((ARRAY[wifi_mac, ethernet_mac, bluetooth_mac]))=({12189697,12189698,12189699}).

The problem in your case is that built-in BTree and GiST indexes don't offer an operator class with &&(array,array) required for this. The gist__int_ops I used above is from intarray extension but it only works with arrays of 32-bit int, while mac addresses are 48-bit or 64-bit, both of which need bigint, or the built-in macaddr, macaddr8.

A somewhat hacky workaround for the lack of &&(array,array) support in GiST and BTree could be to use range types emulating arrays, because GiST offers multirange_ops that has &&(anymultirange,anymultirange):
demo2 at db<>fiddle

--below automatically creates mac8_multirange as well
create type public.mac8_range as range(subtype=macaddr8);
--overloading multirange constructor for single-element ranges
create function mac8_multirange(variadic macaddr8[])returns mac8_multirange
immutable leakproof called on null input parallel safe as $$
  select range_agg(case when x is null then 'empty'--avoid '(,)' infinite range
                   else public.mac8_range(x,x,'[]') end)
  from unnest($1)x; $$ language sql;

alter table device add constraint mac_unique_across_3_columns
exclude using gist (mac8_multirange(wifi_mac, ethernet_mac, bluetooth_mac)
                    multirange_ops with &&);

A multirange of single-element ranges effectively works as a set.

Separate table with an FK

If you're free to modify the schema, extract the mac address info to another table, as suggested by @Dale K:

create type interface_type_enum as enum('bluetooth','ethernet','wifi');
create table network_interface(
  interface_type interface_type_enum, 
  addr macaddr8 unique,---------------mac address now universally unique
  device_id bigint references device(id));
insert into network_interface 
  select v.interface_type::interface_type_enum, v.mac, d.id
  from device as d
  cross join lateral(values('bluetooth',bluetooth_mac),
                           ('ethernet',ethernet_mac),
                           ('wifi',wifi_mac)) as v(interface_type,mac);
alter table device drop column wifi_mac
                  ,drop column ethernet_mac
                  ,drop column bluetooth_mac;

Unless you collect some more data about the network interfaces, it sort of looks like EAV.

One-hot with a value

If we assume that each device in your table has at most one network interface, we can enforce that with a check constraint and guard uniqueness with an expression index that always collapses the 3 values down to the one that's not null:

alter table device 
  add constraint max_1_interface 
    check (num_nulls(wifi_mac,ethernet_mac,bluetooth_mac) >= 2)
 ,add constraint mac_unique_across_3_columns
    exclude (coalesce(wifi_mac,ethernet_mac,bluetooth_mac) with =);

Emulating a unique using a slower exclude..with = is necessary in this scenario if you want this as a constraint (for deferrability, for example). Otherwise, the expression-based unique index would already guard the uniqueness just the same, but as of PostgreSQL v18 it cannot yet become a proper constraint. DDL would fail on syntax stage:

create table device (
   id bigint generated by default as identity primary key
  ,wifi_mac macaddr8
  ,ethernet_mac macaddr8
  ,bluetooth_mac macaddr8
  ,unique((coalesce(wifi_mac,ethernet_mac,bluetooth_mac))) );--syntax error

alter table device 
  add constraint mac_unique_across_3_columns
    unique (coalesce(wifi_mac,ethernet_mac,bluetooth_mac));--syntax error

Two-step constraint definition would fail with an explicit message

create unique index mac_unique_across_3_columns 
  on device(coalesce(wifi_mac,ethernet_mac,bluetooth_mac));
alter table device 
  add constraint mac_unique_across_3_columns
    unique using index mac_unique_across_3_columns;
--Cannot create a primary key or unique constraint using such an index.

Constraint trigger

The idea from @Bending Rodriguez isn't entirely wrong: custom equality can also be enforced by a constraint trigger. It's big and ugly but it works:

create function trgf_mac_address_unique_in_3_columns()returns trigger as
$f$ begin
if new.wifi_mac in (new.ethernet_mac, new.bluetooth_mac)
or new.bluetooth_mac=new.ethernet_mac
or exists(select from device where wifi_mac in (new.ethernet_mac, new.bluetooth_mac))
or exists(select from device where bluetooth_mac in (new.ethernet_mac, new.wifi_mac))
or exists(select from device where ethernet_mac in (new.bluetooth_mac, new.wifi_mac))
then raise exception using
    message = format('%s on table %I violates foreign key constraint %I'
                     , TG_OP, TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_NAME),
    errcode = 'foreign_key_violation', -- sqlstate 23503
    schema  = TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,
    table   = TG_TABLE_NAME,
    column  = 'fk_id',
    detail  = format('violating row of %I was %L'
                     , TG_TABLE_NAME, NEW); 
end if;
return new;--doesn't matter if you return `null` or `new` in an `after` trigger
end $f$ language plpgsql;

create constraint trigger ctrg_mac_address_unique_in_3_columns
after insert or update on device 
for each row when(3>num_nulls(new.wifi_mac,new.ethernet_mac,new.bluetooth_mac))
execute function trgf_mac_address_unique_in_3_columns();

insert into device values(default,null,null,'ba:00:01:ff:fe:ba:00:01');

ERROR:  INSERT on table device violates foreign key constraint ctrg_mac_address_unique_in_3_columns
DETAIL:  violating row of device was '(2,,,ba:00:01:ff:fe:ba:00:01)'
CONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL function trgf_mac_address_unique_in_3_columns() line 12 at RAISE

Regular unique constraints on each column guard against same-column duplicates by scanning their corresponding index. This trigger adds scans for the values from the other two columns and checks for duplicates within the incoming row itself.

You could also collect all existing mac addresses in another table with a unique constraint on its single column, by setting up triggers to mirror all insert, update, delete and truncate on your main table. If you think about it, it's close to the version with an added (id,type,mac) table, but it trades the two columns for four triggers.

Q: How to fill NaN value of date time based on another column +1? A:

I would recommend that you set up a list of months eg. months='Jan', 'Feb, 'Mar' etc., and then use a simple algorithm to change month (and possibly year) eg.

dateIn="11 Mar 2011"   #the data comes into this variable
dateIn=dateIn.split(" ")#changes to ["11","Mar","2011"] which is easier to work with
day, month, year= dateIn[0], dateIn[1], int(dateIn[2])#gets the parts of the date seperated

if month == months[len(months)-1]: #last month so we change the year
    year+=1 #add to year
    month=months[0] #reset month
else:
    #is not the last month
    for m in months:
        if m == month:
            month=months[months.index(month)-1] #finds the next month and updates the month
dateOut=f"{day} {month} {year}" #reformats to an output (in this case "11 Apr 2011")

The input and output would need to be delt with (I don't know how your dataset works) and you would probably want to change this to a function but it would work for you.

Q: Docker compose postgres instance suddenly stopped working A:

Compose healthcheck: has two forms. If you specify test: ["CMD", ...] then you are responsible for breaking the command into words; if you specify test: ["CMD-SHELL", ...] then Docker wraps the command in sh -c. The environment variable expansion requires a shell, and you should change CMD to CMD-SHELL. A bare string defaults to CMD-SHELL and that's easier still.

healthcheck:
  test: pg_isready -d $$POSTGRES_DB

(Also note that you need to double the dollar sign: by default Compose will interpolate environment-variable references using the host system's environment, but you probably want the container's environment here.)
